item.title: Smile for the Camera: The Ethics of Facial Recognition at Pearson Airport
item.description:
Every Time I Land at Pearson

I have been through Pearson Airport more times than I can count. And everytime I get off my flight to go through customs I notice the same thing. You walk up to the kiosk, scan your passport, look into the camera and answer a few questions. A slip prints out. You hand it over to a border officer. They glance at it for maybe three seconds and wave you through.

item.title: Data Ethics in Action: What a Simple Survey Taught me
item.description:
One of my recent assignments put me in the shoes of a data analyst. I was to be given course survey results and asked to review them and make recommendations to help figure out which course needed to be updated or redesigned. Honestly when I first read it I thought it would be pretty straightforward.

But when I actually started reading through the survey something felt off…

A Task That Seemed Simple

The survey told participants were anonymous. But to take the survey they had to log in with their username and password. I was sitting there of a second thinking wait, those two things don’t really go together. If you’re being told to log in with your credentials your credentials your identity is attached to the session. Even if the final report doesn’t show names the system could still technically connect a response to a person through things like log in records, user ids, or time stamps. That’s not really anonymous, just anonymous looking and I think there’s a difference.

item.title: Designing My Future Through Data & AI
item.description:
Starting My Journey in Data & AI

Hi, I’m Alyssa! I’m currently studying Data Analytics & AI, and I’m excited to be in a field that blends logic, creativity and real-world impact. What I love most about this program is how versatile it is. Data is everywhere, and the ability to analyze it opens doors in almost every industry imaginable.

Where My Passion Meets My Purpose

For me, the most exciting application of data analytics is sports. Football specifically. I’ve always been passionate about the game, and the idea that I can use skills like data visualization, predictive modeling and AI to uncover patterns in player performance or game strategy feels like the perfect intersection of who I am and what I’m learning. It’s what made me realize this field was the right fit.
